findings.explanation: The kana name reads Rokuro-ya or Rokuroya: ろくろ is rokuro and 屋 is ya. 'Rokuya' drops the second ro and changes the shop name.
findings.japanese:
「来月、楽しみにしてるからね～。
わたし今ろくろ屋のバウムクーヘンにハマってんだ。
西急の地下にあるんだけどいっつも１時間待ちで」
findings.todokanai: "That's because I'm looking forward to next month. Right now I'm completely addicted to the baumkuchen they sell at Rokuya. It's in the basement of Seikyu, though there's always an hour-long queue there."

findings.highlight: Kizaki-san has been really stiff ever since his marriage was decided on.
findings.evidenceJa: 木崎さんも結婚決めちゃって食いつき悪くなった
findings.explanation: Since Kizaki decided to marry, he no longer bites at or shows much interest in Matsuoka's chocolate-count competition. 'Stiff' describes demeanor rather than his reduced engagement with the game.
findings.japanese:
「だって浜田さんは娘にもらったチョコ自慢しかしないし、
木崎さんも結婚決めちゃって食いつき悪くなったしさぁ、
勝負できそうなのお前ぐらいしかいないんだよ」
findings.todokanai: "Because Hamada-san doesn't brag about anything except for the chocolate he got from his daughter. Kizaki-san has been really stiff ever since his marriage was decided on. The only person I can compete against is you."

findings.highlight: Had you sucked up to Mari-san as much as he did
findings.evidenceJa: あんただって麻理さんに頭下げてお願いしてたらとことんまで鍛えてくれた
findings.explanation: Suzuki says Mari would have trained Matsuoka thoroughly too if he had bowed his head and asked her. The translation adds that Haruki sucked up to Mari, degrading a relationship the source does not characterize that way.
findings.japanese:
「二年先輩がこの言い草…
あんただって麻理さんに頭下げてお願いしてたら
とことんまで鍛えてくれたのに」
findings.todokanai: "Is that something a second-year senior should be saying? Had you sucked up to Mari-san as much as he did, she'd have trained you too."

findings.highlight: I'll get back to my work!
findings.evidenceJa: 出先行ってきます！今日はそのまま直帰ですから
findings.explanation: Haruki announces that he is heading out to an external work destination and will go straight home from there. The translation says he is returning to work, making the following direct-return declaration incoherent.
findings.japanese:
「出先行ってきます！
今日はそのまま直帰ですから！」
findings.todokanai: "I'll get back to my work! Once I'm done, I'm going straight home!"

findings.highlight: I feel like I'm going to have a bad time
findings.evidenceJa: 痛くも無くない腹を探られるかもしれないから
findings.explanation: Haruki fears they will probe a belly that is not entirely pain-free: unlike the idiom's innocent person, he really does have secrets to uncover. The translation reduces this guilt-laden risk to a generic bad time.
findings.japanese:
今日の浮かれた日に、この人たちに付き合ってると、
痛くも無くない腹を探られるかもしれないから
さっさと職場から逃げ出した。
findings.todokanai: If I spend any more time with these people on a day as festive as today, I feel like I'm going to have a bad time, so I run away from my post.

findings.evidenceJa: 手首に少し痛みが出た
findings.explanation: Youko's cover story specifically locates post-concert pain in Kazusa's wrist. The translation broadens it to the hand, changing a concrete medical detail during hostile press questioning.
findings.japanese:
「いいえ、そのようなことはありません。
確かに前回公演後、手首に少し痛みが出たようですが、
現在は完治していますので」
findings.todokanai: "No, that's not true. She did indeed have minor pains in her hand after her last concert, but it is fully healed by now."

findings.highlight: Her special number will be released after the next issue of Ensemble.
findings.evidenceJa: 今度アンサンブルから彼女の特集号が出る
findings.explanation: Youko promotes an upcoming special or feature issue on Kazusa from Ensemble. The translation calls it a 'special number' and says it will appear after the next issue, adding a release sequence absent from 今度.
findings.japanese:
「あらご存じ？
今度アンサンブルから彼女の特集号が出るんですのよ？
記事の中でも是非取り上げてくださると嬉しいですわ」
findings.todokanai: "Ah, so you're aware? Her special number will be released after the next issue of Ensemble. I'd be thrilled if you could write about it in your article."

findings.highlight: I thought it'd be fine if it was just for a short while.
findings.evidenceJa: 昨日までは短い時間なら問題ないと言ってた
findings.explanation: Miyoko says that through yesterday Kazusa herself had said a short interview would be no problem. The translation makes the approval Miyoko's own judgment, obscuring why she accepted despite Youko's warning.
findings.japanese:
「本当に申し訳ありません。
昨日までは短い時間なら問題ないと言ってたので…」
findings.todokanai: "I'm really sorry. Up until yesterday, I thought it'd be fine if it was just for a short while."

findings.highlight: I sent a text not to "Setsuna," but "Sakamoto Sumiki."
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が選んだ通話先は、『雪菜』じゃなくて『坂本純生』だった
findings.explanation: Haruki chooses whom to call, not whom to text; the voicemail content will carry Kazusa's numeric code. Changing the medium breaks the established answering-service mechanism. The given-name reading 'Sumiki' also remains unverified from source-only kanji.
findings.japanese:
そんな思いに耽りながら俺が選んだ通話先は、
『雪菜』じゃなくて『坂本純生』だった。
findings.todokanai: While indulging myself in these thoughts, I sent a text not to "Setsuna," but "Sakamoto Sumiki."

findings.highlight: At night, we made love tenderly and kissed.
findings.evidenceJa: 夜は優しく抱きあって、キスをしあってた
findings.explanation: At night Haruki and Kazusa tenderly held one another and kissed. 抱きあう here states mutual embracing; translating it as 'made love' asserts nightly sex the source does not specify.
findings.japanese:
昼間は普段の生活を取り戻してた。
夜は優しく抱きあって、キスをしあってた。
findings.todokanai: During the day, she had returned to playing the piano and going about her normal life. At night, we made love tenderly and kissed.

findings.highlight: my head alone pretended to "not be there."
findings.evidenceJa: 頭だけが『ここじゃない』と必死に抵抗してた
findings.explanation: As his limbs make him leave the train, Haruki's mind desperately resists by insisting 'this isn't the place.' The translation says his head pretends not to be there, losing the conflict over getting off one stop early.
findings.japanese:
勝手に降りようとする手足に対して
頭だけが『ここじゃない』と必死に抵抗してた。
findings.todokanai: My feet forced themselves to get off the train, but my head alone pretended to "not be there."

findings.evidenceJa: あたし、別に…なんでもないよ
findings.explanation: Kazusa tries to dismiss her condition and the call as nothing—she is fine, nothing is the matter. The translation says she has no wants, turning denial of distress into a denial of desire.
findings.japanese: 「あたし、別に…なんでもないよ」

findings.evidenceJa: 自分をねじ伏せるくらい、なんでもない
findings.explanation: Haruki says forcibly suppressing or overpowering himself is nothing if it protects Kazusa's heart. 'Putting myself down' means belittling himself and loses his choice to crush his own competing will.
findings.japanese:
かずさの心を守るためには、
自分をねじ伏せるくらい、なんでもない。
findings.todokanai: Putting myself down for the sake of protecting Kazusa's heart is nothing to me.
